# TENSA — API map for LLM agents

TENSA is a web workbench + HTTP/WebSocket API around the ANDES power-system
simulator. Everything the UI does goes through this API, so an agent can do
everything a human can. No authentication: the server trusts the local user and
binds to 127.0.0.1 by default.

Base URL: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api  (all routes below are relative to /api)
Full machine-readable contract: GET /openapi.json  (Swagger UI at /docs, ReDoc at /redoc)
Copy-paste examples: examples/ in the repo (curl walkthrough + Python client).

## Golden workflow (order matters)

1. POST /sessions                          → {"session_id": "..."}  (one ANDES System per session, isolated subprocess)
2. POST /sessions/{id}/case                {"primary_path": "ieee14/ieee14_full.xlsx"}  — path is RELATIVE to the server's --workspace dir (put a file there with POST /workspace/files); formats: xlsx raw dyr json m; optional "addfiles": ["...dyr"]
3. (pre-setup only) POST /sessions/{id}/disturbances  — add faults/toggles/alters BEFORE running anything
4. POST /sessions/{id}/pflow               → converged flag + bus voltages; or POST /sessions/{id}/tds {"tf": 5.0} for time-domain (batch, synchronous)
                                             pflow also returns, per line, P/Q at both ends, the loss and the loading in % of rate_a (null when unrated),
                                             per generator, its Q limits in MVAr, and a "summary" (generation, load, shunts, losses, slack output)
                                             optional body, for that run only: {"tolerance": 1e-6, "max_iterations": 25, "flat_start": false,
                                             "enforce_q_limits": false}. Q limits are reported, not enforced, unless enforce_q_limits is true or the case
                                             file turns them on; false turns that off. Left-out settings keep the case's own.
                                             "settings" in the response is what the run used. If it did not converge, retry with a higher
                                             max_iterations, flat_start true, or a looser tolerance.
5. GET  /sessions/{id}/operating-point     → PflowResult: bus_voltages/bus_angles dicts (keyed by bus idx),
                                             line_flows, generator_outputs, load_consumption
6. POST /sessions/{id}/reload              → back to pre-setup state (required to add MORE disturbances after a run)
7. DELETE /sessions/{id}                   → cleanup

Key state rule: a session is "pre-setup" after case load / reload, and "setup" after the
first PF/TDS run. Disturbances and topology edits (add/edit/delete elements) are
REJECTED with 409 once setup has happened — the error's "recovery" field tells you to reload.

## Errors

All errors are RFC-7807 ProblemDetails JSON: {type, title, status, detail, recovery}.
"recovery" is machine-actionable: {kind: load-case | reload-case | run-pflow | retry |
add-measurements | wait-for-job | wait-for-sweep | none, label: "..."}. Follow it.

## Route inventory

Sessions:        POST/GET /sessions · GET/DELETE /sessions/{id}
                 (a session with no request for 180 s is reaped; GET /sessions/{id} counts as one)
Case+topology:   POST /sessions/{id}/case · POST /sessions/{id}/reload · GET /sessions/{id}/topology
                 GET /sessions/{id}/topology/models/{model}/alterable_params · GET /sessions/{id}/connectivity
Power flow:      POST /sessions/{id}/pflow · GET /sessions/{id}/operating-point
TDS:             POST /sessions/{id}/tds  (batch; body: tf, optional h, integrator, tds_config_overrides, dae_vars, controllers)
                 dae_vars: ANDES variables to record, named as ANDES names them ("omega GENROU 1", "vf GENROU 2");
                 their values at every step come back under "traces" ({t, variables:[{name, values}], truncated}):
                 one row per step ANDES solved, at the time it solved it, the last at tf when the run reached it.
                 GET /sessions/{id}/dae-variables[?q=&kind=&model=&limit=&offset=]  (the names a run can record: q is
                 words that must all appear, kind x=state or y=algebraic; needs no run, does not close the case to disturbances)
                 controllers: frequency loops the run closes on batteries and other distributed generation devices
                 (ESD1, PVD1, EV1, EV2). Parameters only, no code. Each is {"type":"droop","model":"ESD1","idx":1,
                 "gain":MW per Hz,"deadband":Hz,"p_max":MW} or {"type":"ffr","model":"ESD1","idx":1,"power":MW,
                 "trigger_deviation":Hz,"trigger_rocof":Hz/s,"hold":s}, with optional "frequency" ("coi": inertia-weighted
                 machine speed, the default; "bus": the device's own measurement), "period" (s between samples, 0.1),
                 "t_start" (s) and "ramp" (MW/s). Powers in MW, positive discharging. The result's "controllers" has,
                 per controller, first_action_t, released_t (ffr), peak_command, final_command and "trace"
                 ({t, frequency, command, output, soc, truncated}, one entry per sample).
                 GET /sessions/{id}/tds/controllers  (the devices of the loaded case a controller can command, each with
                 "p_limit" in MW and "variables": dae_vars names for its command "Pext", frequency "fHz", current and
                 state of charge; "coi_available" false means only "frequency":"bus" works; needs no run)
                 POST /sessions/{id}/abort  (cooperative abort of a running TDS)
Response metrics:POST /response-metrics  (no session; body {"series":[{"name","t":[...],"y":[...]}], optional t_start, t_end,
                 settling_band, rocof_window} -> per series: initial, final, peak, nadir, max_deviation, rocof, settling_time,
                 overshoot_pct, damping {ratio, frequency_hz}; feed it a batch run's "traces")
COMTRADE export: POST /comtrade  (no session; body {"t":[...],"channels":[{"name","values":[...],"unit"}], optional name, station,
                 device, frequency_hz, start_time, trigger_t} -> application/zip holding <name>.cfg and <name>.dat, an
                 IEEE C37.111-1999 record with ASCII data: one analog channel per signal, scaled over its own range, and a
                 time stamp per sample; feed it "t" and "variables" of a batch run's "traces" as they are; "unit" is
                 optional, null values are written as missing; 413 over 5,000,000 values, channels times samples)
Disturbances:    POST/GET /sessions/{id}/disturbances
  FaultSpec:  {"kind":"fault","bus_idx":"7","tf":1.0,"tc":1.1,"xf":0.05,"rf":0}   (3-phase fault at bus, applied tf→tc seconds)
  ToggleSpec: {"kind":"toggle","model":"Line","dev_idx":"Line_6","t":1.0}          (connect/disconnect a device at t)
  AlterSpec:  {"kind":"alter","model":"PQ","dev_idx":"PQ_1","src":"p0","t":1.0,"method":"*","amount":1.2}
              (change parameter at t; method one of + - * / =; use alterable_params to discover valid src names)
Elements:        GET /topology/schema (every buildable model + typed params) · POST /sessions/{id}/elements (add)
                 PUT /sessions/{id}/elements/{model}/{idx} (edit) · DELETE /sessions/{id}/elements/{model}/{idx}[?cascade=true]
                 (delete any element, one the case file brought included; the file is not written. 422 with "dependents" and
                 "disturbances" when other elements name it or disturbances act on it: delete those first, or send cascade=true to
                 delete them with it. The 200 body is the topology plus "deleted" and "disturbances", what went)
                 POST /sessions/{id}/undo-last-edit · POST /sessions/{id}/redo-edit (take back / put back the last add, edit or delete;
                 the topology's "undo" and "redo" name the edit each would act on, null when there is none; a delete put back takes
                 what it took the first time, and is refused with 422 and the list if anything else has come to depend on the element)
                 POST /sessions/{id}/blank (start empty system) · POST /sessions/{id}/save (write case file; format xlsx, json or raw)
Jobs:            GET /sessions/{id}/jobs[?kind=&status=] · GET/DELETE /sessions/{id}/jobs/{job_id}
                 (statuses: pending running done failed cancelled)
Messages:        GET /sessions/{id}/messages[?after=&level=&limit=] · DELETE /sessions/{id}/messages  (what ANDES logged while a command ran:
                 {"messages":[{"seq","time","level","logger","source","text","repeat"}],"first_seq","last_seq","next_after","dropped"};
                 level is info, warning or error, source the command (load_case, run_pflow, run_tds, ...); level=warning returns warnings and
                 errors only; logger tensa.notice marks what the server worked out itself, a generator held at a Q limit or a load turned into an impedance, which ANDES does not log;
                 a message that repeats the newest one is kept once, its repeat count growing; it is then numbered again, so reading on by after returns it with the larger count;
                 paths of the server are not in the text (the workspace is written relative to itself, the home directory as ~, any other absolute path as <path>);
                 pass next_after back as after to read on; a read does not wait for a run in progress)
Clone editing:   POST /sessions/{id}/case/clone (start copy-on-write edit)
                 PUT /sessions/{id}/case/clone/params/{model}/{idx}/{param} (edit one param)
                 POST .../case/clone/undo · .../case/clone/redo · .../case/clone/reset · .../case/clone/save-as
                 GET .../case/clone/diff/{model}/{idx}
Eigenanalysis:   POST /sessions/{id}/eig · GET .../eig/modes/{mode_idx}/participation · GET .../eig/state-matrix.mat
CPF:             POST /sessions/{id}/cpf · POST /sessions/{id}/cpf/qv  (needs a converged pflow; every setting is for that run only)
                 cpf body, all optional: {"direction": "load", "enforce_q_limits": false, "stop_at": "nose", "step": 0.1, "max_iter": 500}
                 direction: load (every load and PV generator in proportion, the default) | load-only (the slack supplies the increase) |
                 gen (PV generators only) | custom, with "load_increase": [{"idx":"PQ_1","p":10,"q":3}] and
                 "generator_increase": [{"idx":2,"p":10}] in MW / MVAr per unit of lambda (the slack cannot be named).
                 With load, load-only and gen, lambda = 1 is twice the base value.
                 step is the first step only: ANDES sizes the rest itself, 0.5 in lambda at most. A custom direction of small increases
                 is therefore a long path (ten times the increases is the same curve at a tenth of the lambda); when done_msg reads
                 "Reached max steps (N)" the run stopped short, and a larger max_iter takes it further.
                 enforce_q_limits true switches a PV or slack generator to PQ at qmin/qmax along the path; solve pflow with
                 enforce_q_limits first, or the answer is 409 when a generator is already past a limit. A generator held at a limit
                 stays held. stop_at full also traces the lower branch back to lambda = 0 (the steps after nose_idx).
                 → lambdas, voltages_per_bus, nose_idx (-1 and truncated true when no nose was reached), max_lam (lambda at the nose),
                 "generators": [{"model","idx","bus","q":[MVAr per step],"q_min","q_max"}], "limit_events":
                 [{"step","lam","model","idx","bus","limit":"qmax|qmin","at_nose","would_release_step"}] (step 0: held by the power flow;
                 at_nose true: the nose is where that generator ran out of reactive power, a limit-induced collapse and not a smooth fold;
                 would_release_step: from that step its voltage is back across the set-point and a real exciter would leave the limit,
                 which ANDES's limiter does not, so the curve from there is the one for a generator pinned at its limit),
                 q_limits_enforced, stop_at, complete (false: a full curve whose lower branch broke off), direction.
                 cpf/qv body: {"bus_idx": "5", "q_range": 5.0, "enforce_q_limits": false}; same response, lambdas holding Q at the bus and max_lam the largest of them.
State estimation:POST /sessions/{id}/se/measurements/generate · POST /sessions/{id}/se
PMU placement:   POST/GET /sessions/{id}/pmu · DELETE /sessions/{id}/pmu/{pmu_idx} · GET .../pmu/{run_id}/export.csv
Profiles:        POST /sessions/{id}/profiles/upload · POST/GET/DELETE /sessions/{id}/profiles
Sweeps:          POST /sessions/{id}/sweep (param sweep over disturbance/sim values; per-iteration TDS results)
Snapshots:       POST /sessions/{id}/snapshot · POST .../snapshot/restore · GET .../snapshots · DELETE .../snapshot/{name}
Bundles:         POST /sessions/{id}/bundle/export (zip: case+disturbances+params) · POST .../bundle/import
Reports:         GET /sessions/{id}/report
Workspace:       GET /workspace/files · GET/PUT /workspace/layout?case_path=<rel>
                 POST /workspace/files?name=<file>[&overwrite=true]  (adds a case file; the body IS the file's bytes
                 as in curl --data-binary @ieee14.raw ..., not multipart, which answers 415; 32 MiB; xlsx raw dyr json m;
                 409 if the name exists and overwrite is not true; a <case>.layout.json name is refused, PUT /workspace/layout writes those)
Version:         GET /version  → {"tensa": "...", "andes": "..."}  (installed package versions, no session needed)
Health:          GET /health  → {"status": "ok", "version", "andes_version", "sessions": {"active", "max"},
                 "cache": {"state": ready|unchecked|missing, "warm", "generating"}}  (poll it; no session, never waits for a worker;
                 "cache" is ANDES's generated code: until it is ready, the first case load may take 30 s or more)

## WebSockets (live streaming)

Protocol for all WS endpoints: connect → server sends {"type":"ready"} → client sends its
first command frame. Close codes: 4404 unknown session, 4500 worker error.

WS /api/ws/{session_id}            — TDS live stream. Send {"type":"start_tds","tf":5.0}, optionally with
                                     "vars" (groups bus_v gen_state gen_power line_flow load_pq), "dae_vars" (ANDES
                                     variable names, each one more column named as given) and "controllers" (as on
                                     POST /tds; the "done" frame then carries "controllers" without the traces);
                                     server replies {"type":"stream_start",...} (metadata.var_columns
                                     names the columns once) then BINARY Apache Arrow IPC chunks, one
                                     per frame, each with a "t" column and a "v" list column holding
                                     the row's values in var_columns order, then {"type":"done",...}.
                                     A row is a step ANDES solved, at the time it solved it (the rows are
                                     ANDES's own dae.ts); the last is at tf when the run reached it.
                                     With "decimation":"mean" and "max_rate_hz":N a row is the mean of the
                                     steps of each 1/N s, and the last row is still the run's last step.
                                     Reconnect+resume: {"type":"resume","run_id":"...","last_seq":N}.
                                     A client that falls too far behind the run, or resumes past the
                                     ~30 s buffer, gets {"type":"resync",...} and the socket closes;
                                     its "cause" is "client_lagged" or "buffer_evicted" ("reason"
                                     says it in words). The run itself is never slowed by a client.
WS /api/ws/{session_id}/jobs/events— job lifecycle feed: "snapshot" then "job" envelopes per transition.
WS /api/ws/{session_id}/sweep/{id} — sweep progress per iteration.

Prefer batch POST /tds unless you need live data — it returns complete results in one
response and needs no Arrow decoding.

## Gotchas for agents

- Case paths are workspace-relative; absolute paths and ".." are rejected (400).
- A request with a JSON body must send "Content-Type: application/json": the json= argument of
  httpx and requests does, but curl -d and requests' data= do not. Without it the body is not
  parsed and the route answers 422.
- GENROU machines: ANDES uses M (=2H); the add-element endpoint accepts H and converts.
- Exciters/governors link to machines via the "syn" parameter (a SynGen idx).
- A reference to another device ("bus", "gen", "syn") may be sent as "5" or 5: the add and edit routes match it
  to the idx the case holds.
- An add that leaves out a parameter ANDES has no default for ("gen" of a GENROU) is a 422 and adds nothing.
- ESD1 battery: needs "bus", "gen" (a PV or Slack on the same bus, which it takes over when TDS starts; that
  generator's p0 is the power it starts at, negative to charge) and "pqflag" (1 = active power has priority).
  "Sn" defaults to the system base (topology "base_mva"); keep it there: pmx/qmx/qmn/ialim are pu of Sn while the
  set-point and the output are pu of the system base. The state of charge is the dae var "pIG_y ESD1 <idx>"
  (name it in dae_vars); it moves by the delivered MW over En (MWh) each hour. Step the power during a run with
  an Alter on "Pext0" (system-base pu, added to the set-point), or have it follow the frequency with a TDS
  "controllers" entry. Not both on one battery: a controller writes "Pext0" at every sample, so a run with an
  Alter on the same device's "Pext0" is a 422 (an Alter on "pref0" is fine).
- TDS controllers act on distributed generation devices only. A synchronous machine's governor is not a target.
  With a p_max left out a droop is limited to what the device can deliver ("p_limit" of the listing).
- A TDS run that goes on from where the last one stopped (a larger tf) with the same "controllers" keeps their
  state: an ffr that has fired does not fire again. A reload or a restored snapshot starts them afresh, so an ffr
  that fired before the snapshot was taken can fire again in a run that goes on from it.
- Line/Transformer impedances are pu on (Sn, Vn1); the add-element endpoint derives
  Vn1/Vn2 from the connected buses automatically.
- TDS batch endpoint is synchronous with a 300 s server-side cap; for long runs use the WS stream.
- After any run, GET /operating-point reflects the final state (TDS end point, not the initial PF).
- A run that converged can still carry warnings (a device whose initialisation failed, a limit ANDES did not adjust). After an odd
  result, GET /sessions/{id}/messages?level=warning shows what ANDES said about it.
- Snapshots restore by replay (reload the case, re-add the recorded disturbances, setup, PF). The
  ANDES solver-state blob is opt-in on both ends: "include_dill": true on POST .../snapshot writes it
  and "use_dill_optimization": true on POST .../snapshot/restore tries it first.
- model names are ANDES model names: Bus, Line, PQ, PV, Slack, Shunt, GENROU, GENCLS,
  IEEEX1, ESDC2A, EXST1, SEXS, TGOV1, IEEEG1, ESD1, Fault, Toggle, Alter, ...
  GET /api/topology/schema lists every model the builder supports with typed params.

## MCP

An MCP (Model Context Protocol) stdio server ships as an optional extra:
  pip install -e './server[mcp]' && tensa mcp --workspace ~/andes-cases
It wraps the golden workflow (create_session, load_case, run_pflow, run_tds,
add_disturbance, get_topology, get_operating_point, list_workspace_files, ...) so MCP
clients (Claude Code, etc.) can drive simulations as native tools.
